movie_title: Why Are 6 Countries Fighting Over the South China Sea?
introduction: In this video, we retrace on maps the evolution of the conflict that today confronts six opposing co
lead_intro: Discover the historical origins and complex evolution of the South China Sea conflict involving multiple countries. From territorial claims to military bases, this region has a rich and tumultuous history.

quiz.question: Which country has built military bases, ports, and airports on artificial islets in the South China Sea?
quiz.explanation: In the South China Sea, China has constructed military bases, ports, and airports on artificial islets it created by dredging sand from underwater.

quiz.question: What type of rich resource found in the surrounding seabeds revived interest in the Spratly archipelagos in the late 1960s?
quiz.explanation: Reports of rich oil and gas resources in the surrounding seabeds of the Spratly archipelagos reignited interest in the region in the late 1960s.

quiz.question: In 1982, what did the United Nations establish to define maritime boundaries and prevent conflicts over seabed resources?
choices: Convention on the Law of the Sea
quiz.answer: Convention on the Law of the Sea
quiz.explanation: The United Nations created the Convention on the Law of the Sea in 1982 to set maritime boundaries and avoid conflicts over seabed resources among nations.

quiz.question: Which country took the matter of Chinese actions in the Scarborough Shoal to the Permanent Court of Arbitration at The Hague?
quiz.explanation: The Philippines reacted to Chinese actions in the Scarborough Shoal by bringing the matter to the Permanent Court of Arbitration at The Hague.

quiz.question: Which major player in the South China Sea region stepped up its military presence to ensure free navigation in the sea?
quiz.explanation: The United States increased its military presence in the South China Sea to guarantee free navigation in the region.
